summary: ComputeTempSphere::init() detects a temp/region bias with an exact strcmp on tbias->style, which no longer matches once the bias compute is promoted to 'temp/region/kk', so tempbias stays 1 and dof_compute() calls tbias->dof_remove(-1), reading atom->x[-1] out of bounds.
evidence: src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:106-109 'if (strcmp(tbias->style, "temp/region") == 0) tempbias = 2; else tempbias = 1;'.  src/modify.cpp:1267-1272 rewrites the style string when a suffix is applied: 'std::string estyle = arg[2] + std::string("/") + lmp->non_pair_suffix(); ... compute[ncompute]->style = utils::strdup(estyle);' so the style is literally "temp/region/kk".  src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:181-182 then takes the tempbias==1 branch: 'if (mode == ALL) dof -= tbias->dof_remove(-1) * natoms_temp;' and src/compute_temp_region.cpp:89-94 'int ComputeTempRegion::dof_remove(int i) { double *x = atom->x[i]; if (region->match(x[0], x[1], x[2])) return 0; return 1; }' dereferences atom->x[-1].  The new src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_region_kokkos.h:16-18 registers temp/region/kk, making this reachable for the first time (there is no /omp or /gpu temp/region).  The identical strcmp appears in ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.cpp:122 and BODY/compute_temp_body.cpp:113.
failure_scenario: lmp -sf kk with 'compute b all temp/region myreg' and 'compute t all temp/sphere bias b': the bias compute becomes temp/region/kk, tempbias is set to 1 instead of 2, dof_compute() calls dof_remove(-1) which indexes atom->x[-1] (garbage pointer -> segfault or nonsense), and the per-atom region DOF subtraction is silently skipped so the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compare utils::strip_style_suffix(tbias->style, lmp) with "temp/region" in compute_temp_sphere.cpp (and the same lines in compute_temp_asphere.cpp / compute_temp_body.cpp); optionally also guard dof_remove(-1) in ComputeTempRegion.

summary: In the host/device force-overlap path the forces a non-KOKKOS (legacy Host) force style writes into atom->f are never transferred into the Kokkos host buffer before the merge, so on builds where k_f needs a transform view they are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:421-424 sets 'datamask_exclude = (F_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK)' whenever overlap_possible(), and 438/441 (and 467/470, 502/505) then use only the masked forms '~(~datamask_read|datamask_exclude)', so F_MASK is never passed to atomKK->modified() after the style ran.  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.cpp:210-213 shows modified(Host, mask) only calls 'k_f.modify_host()' when the mask contains F_MASK, so TransformView::modified_legacy_hostkk stays 0.  The merge at verlet_kokkos.cpp:513-514 is 'atomKK->k_f.sync_legacy_to_hostkk(); Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),f_merge_copy,atomKK->k_f.view_hostkk());' and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:955-968 makes sync_legacy_to_hostkk() a no-op unless modified_legacy_hostkk is set.  A non-KOKKOS style has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128, src/kspace.cpp:98, src/bond.cpp:62) and writes atom->f, which memory_kokkos.h:119 aliases to k_f.view_host() (the legacy view), a different allocation from view_hostkk() whenever TransformView::NEED_TRANSFORM is true (kokkos_type.h:700) -- i.e. single-precision builds (KK_ACC_FLOAT=float, kokkos_type.h:401-402) or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT builds.  host_force_styles() (verlet_kokkos.cpp:699) deliberately accepts Host as well as HostKK, so the path is taken for such styles.  Contrast the sibling DynamicalMatrixKokkos::update_force (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:287), which merges from k_f.view_host() (the legacy view) instead.
failure_scenario: GPU backend, single-precision KOKKOS build (or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT), '-sf kk' with any force style that has no /kk variant (e.g. a non-KOKKOS kspace such as pppm/cg, or an unported pair/bond style): that style's entire force contribution is added to a buffer nobody reads, the merge adds zeros, and the trajectory is silently wrong. In the non-overlap (CPU-only) path datamask_exclude is 0 and F_MASK is claimed normally, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Claim the legacy write before the merge (e.g. call atomKK->k_f.modify_legacy_hostkk() in the execute_on_host block when any host force style has execution_space == Host), or merge from k_f.view_host() as DynamicalMatrixKokkos does; note that when both a Host and a HostKK style contributed the two buffers must be added, not deep-copied over each other.

summary: alpha_step() and the x0 snapshot treat xvec as a flat 3*nlocal alias of atom->x, which is only valid for LayoutRight; unlike every other loop in the min/kk styles these three kernels have no F_LAYOUTRIGHT branch, so a KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default GPU build moves the wrong coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:108-109 'if (nvec) xvec = DAT::t_kkfloat_1d(d_x.data(),nvec); if (nvec) fvec = DAT::t_kkacc_1d(d_f.data(),nvec);' aliases the (nmax,3) view k_x as a flat length-3*nlocal view.  The three loops that use it are unguarded: :252-254 'Kokkos::parallel_for(nvec, LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i) { l_x0[i] = l_xvec[i]; });', :391-393 'l_xvec[i] = l_x0[i];' and :410-412 'l_xvec[i] += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(alpha)*l_h[i];'.  Everywhere else the same file and its subclasses do branch, precisely because the flat alias is layout-dependent: min_kokkos.h:27 'static constexpr int F_LAYOUTRIGHT = std::is_same<LMPDeviceLayout,Kokkos::LayoutRight>::value;', min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:191-204 and :286-304, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:68-86, :125-143 and :178-196, min_kokkos.cpp:624-636/661-673/698-711.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:177-185 defines LMPDeviceLayout as Kokkos::LayoutRight only for LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_LEGACY; with '-D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default' (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:33-40) it becomes LMPDeviceType::array_layout, i.e. Kokkos::LayoutLeft on CUDA/HIP.  Under LayoutLeft the flat view of length 3*nlocal covers x(0..3*nlocal-1, 0) -- the x-components of the first 3*nlocal atoms including ghosts -- not (x,y,z) of the first nlocal atoms.
failure_scenario: cmake -D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default with a CUDA/HIP backend and 'min_style cg/kk': the line search snapshots and restores only x-components (of owned and ghost atoms) and adds alpha*h into those slots, so y and z are never stepped and ghost x-coordinates are corrupted. The minimization silently converges to garbage; with LAYOUT=legacy (the default) the code is correct, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Give these three loops the same 'if constexpr (F_LAYOUTRIGHT) ... else' treatment as the fvec loops, indexing atomKK->k_x.view_device()(i,0..2) with j = 3*i in the LayoutLeft branch; do the same for the xvec loops in min_quickmin_kokkos/min_fire_kokkos, or reject KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default in MinKokkos::init().

summary: compute_scalar()/compute_vector() always call the host-facing tbias->remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() instead of the kokkosable-guarded *_kk() variants, forcing a device->host->device round trip of v on every invocation even when the bias compute is a KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:52-58 and 79-84 (and 126-132, 153-158): 'atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); atomKK->sync(execution_space, V_MASK);'.  For a kk bias, e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_ramp_kokkos.cpp:167-171, remove_bias_all() is 'remove_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK);' -- an unconditional full copy of v to the host.  Every other KOKKOS caller uses the guarded form, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:136 'if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();' and fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:212/371, fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:353.
failure_scenario: compute temp/sphere/kk with 'bias' pointing at a temp/ramp/kk or temp/region/kk compute on a GPU build: every thermo evaluation copies the full v array device->host and back, which is exactly the per-step transfer the KOKKOS package policy forbids. Results are still correct, only slow.
suggested_fix: Follow the package pattern: 'if (tbias->kokkosable) tbias->remove_bias_all_kk(); else { atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); }' and likewise for restore.

summary: s_KK_double2, the reduction type used for every force dot product in the KOKKOS minimizers, stores its two accumulators as KK_FLOAT, which is 'float' in single- and mixed-precision builds, so the global sums lose precision even when the forces themselves are double.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.h:22-23 'struct s_KK_double2 { KK_FLOAT d0, d1;'.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-409 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef float KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef double KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for the mixed setting LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE.  It is used as the parallel_reduce value type over all local degrees of freedom in src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:288-303 (fh in linemin_quadratic), :444-459 (compute_dir_deriv) and src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:127-143 (the CG force tolerance and Polak-Ribiere beta), e.g. 'sdot.d0 += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(l_fvec[i]*l_fvec[i]);' where l_fvec is KK_ACC_FLOAT.  Every other reduction in the same files deliberately accumulates in double: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:193-195 'LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i, double& fdothme)', :228-230, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:214-216, and min_kokkos.cpp:626-635/663-672/700-710.
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (the recommended GPU setting) with min_style cg/kk on a few hundred thousand atoms: dotall[0] and dotall[1] are float sums of ~10^6 terms, so beta = MAX(0.0,(dotall[0]-dotall[1])/gg) and the ftol test lose roughly all digits past 1e-7 relative, degrading or stalling convergence, while the same run in double precision converges.
suggested_fix: Declare d0 and d1 as double (the struct is already named double2) so the reduction accumulates in double regardless of the KK_FLOAT setting.

summary: The per-iteration force dot products of cg/kk, sd/kk and the line-search backtracking loop read the device force view without syncing it, and MinKokkos::energy_force() only pushes host-computed forces to the device when force->newton is set or a min_post_force fix exists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.cpp:524-528 'if (force->newton) { comm->reverse_comm(); timer->stamp(Timer::COMM); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); }' and :538-543 'if (modify->n_min_post_force) { ... modify->min_post_force(vflag); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); ... }' are the only places energy_force() brings f to the device.  A force style without a /kk variant has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128) and datamask_modify == ALL_MASK (pair.cpp), so min_kokkos.cpp:469 'atomKK->modified(force->pair->execution_space,force->pair->datamask_modify);' leaves the newest f on the host only.  The consumers then read the device view with no sync: src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:125-143 (dotall[0]/dotall[1] -> the ftol test and the Polak-Ribiere beta), src/KOKKOS/min_sd_kokkos.cpp:51-64 (set_search_direction, called at :126 after linemin), and src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:286-304 (the fh reduce inside the backtracking while loop).  The omission is inconsistent inside the same files: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:180 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK|F_MASK);' before the loop and :432 'atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK);' in compute_dir_deriv do sync, and the damped-dynamics styles resync every iteration (min_quickmin_kokkos.cpp:116, min_fire_kokkos.cpp:143).
failure_scenario: 'newton off' plus '-sf kk' with a force style that has no KOKKOS version (so f is computed on the host and never reverse-communicated): min_style cg/kk computes beta and the TWO-norm ftol test from a stale device force array, while fnorm_max()/fnorm_sqr() called two lines later do sync and see the correct forces -- the search direction is wrong and the run converges to the wrong configuration or stalls.
suggested_fix: Add atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK) immediately before the reduce in MinCGKokkos::iterate and MinSDKokkos::set_search_direction and inside the backtracking loop of linemin_quadratic, or make MinKokkos::energy_force() sync F_MASK to the device unconditionally at its end.

summary: The class re-declares 'class AtomKokkos *atomKK;' as a private member, shadowing Pointers::atomKK (a reference bound to lmp->atomKK), unlike every other KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.h:81-82 ' private:\n  class AtomKokkos *atomKK;'.  src/pointers.h:131 declares 'class AtomKokkos *&atomKK;' bound to lmp->atomKK (pointers.h:92).  The constructor's 'atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom;' (compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:36) therefore writes the shadowing member instead of lmp->atomKK.  No other file in src/KOKKOS declares an atomKK member (grep 'AtomKokkos \*atomKK' src/KOKKOS/*.h returns only this one).
failure_scenario: Harmless today because atom and lmp->atomKK are the same object, but the member is uninitialized until the derived constructor body runs and any future base-class code path that runs before it (or that reads Pointers::atomKK) sees a different pointer than this class uses.
suggested_fix: Delete the member declaration and use the inherited Pointers::atomKK like the rest of the package.

summary: VerletKokkos::operator()(const int&) and the 'f' view member are dead code -- the force merge uses the free ForceAdder functor, and nothing ever launches a kernel with *this.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.h:41-49 declares 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator() (const int& i) const {f(i,0) += f_merge_copy(i,0); ...}' and 'DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3 f_merge_copy,f;'.  The only merge in the .cpp is verlet_kokkos.cpp:515-516 'Kokkos::parallel_for(atomKK->k_f.extent(0), ForceAdder<DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3,DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_f.view_device(),f_merge_copy));' using the file-static ForceAdder (verlet_kokkos.cpp:36-48); 'f' is only ever assigned (verlet_kokkos.cpp:512 'f = atomKK->k_f.view_device();') and never read.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; the member keeps a reference to the force view alive and the unused operator() invites confusion about which functor the merge uses.
suggested_fix: Remove the operator() and the 'f' member (and the assignment at verlet_kokkos.cpp:512), keeping only f_merge_copy.

summary: NBinKokkos::c_bincount is declared const and is never initialized (so it is permanently an empty view and makes the class non-copy-assignable), and c_bins is assigned only on a regrow and never read.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.h:51 'const typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_bincount;' and :53 'typename AT::t_int_2d_const c_bins;'.  c_bins is written once at src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.cpp:157 'c_bins = bins;' and neither member is read anywhere: the consumers use their own copies, see src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:220-222 and :316 'bincount(_bincount),c_bincount(_bincount),bins(_bins),c_bins(_bins),' fed from src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:104-105 'k_bincount = nbKK->k_bincount; k_bins = nbKK->k_bins;'.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today; the const member silently deletes NBinKokkos's copy-assignment operator, so any future code that assigns one of these objects fails to compile for a non-obvious reason.
suggested_fix: Delete both members (or, if they are meant to be used, drop the const qualifier and assign them wherever bins/bincount are refreshed, including NBinKokkos::bin_atoms_setup).

summary: The pass that measures the maximum bin occupancy increments k_bincount without zeroing it first, so it counts the previous neighbor build's occupancy on top of the current one and over-allocates the bins array by about a factor of two.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:142-148 'atoms_per_bin = 0; copymode = 1; NPairSSAKokkosBinIDAtomsFunctor<DeviceType> f(*this); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal, f, atoms_per_bin);' and the kernel at :279-280 'const int ac = Kokkos::atomic_fetch_add(&(bincount[ibin]), (int)1); if (update <= ac) update = ac + 1;'.  Nothing zeroes bincount before this: bin_atoms_setup() (:61-91) only reallocates k_bincount when mbins grows past k_bins.view_host().extent(0) (:63-69), and the only zeroing is the MemsetZeroFunctor at :205-207, which runs AFTER the reduce, right before the real binning pass at :212-215.  bincount is therefore left holding the previous build's final per-bin counts.  Contrast the ghost counting pass at :157-166, which does zero its counter first ('for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) k_gbincount.view_host()(i) = 0; k_gbincount.modify_host(); k_gbincount.sync<DeviceType>();').  The CPU sibling src/DPD-REACT/nbin_ssa.cpp:63-65 likewise clears binhead[] before every build.
failure_scenario: Any run using neigh_modify binsize / pair_style dpd with nbin ssa/kk: from the second neighbor build on, atoms_per_bin reported by the reduce is about 2*max_bin_occupancy, and src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:200-204 allocates k_bins as (mbins, atoms_per_bin), i.e. roughly double the memory it needs. Results stay correct because binAtomsItem() re-counts from a zeroed bincount.
suggested_fix: Run the MemsetZeroFunctor (or Kokkos::deep_copy(bincount,0)) on k_bincount before the binIDAtomsItem reduce as well, mirroring the k_gbincount reset used for the ghost pass.

summary: NBinSSAKokkos allocates and initializes d_resize/h_resize and declares c_binID/c_bins/c_gbins, none of which are ever read by anything.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.h:48 'typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_binID;' (never assigned), :55 'c_bins' and :62 'c_gbins' (assigned only at src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:196 'c_gbins = gbins;' and :224 'c_bins = bins;'), :64-65 'd_resize'/'h_resize' (allocated at nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:38/45 and set at :52 'h_resize() = 1;', then never touched again).  The consumer keeps its own copies: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87-93 takes only atoms_per_bin, k_bincount, k_bins, ghosts_per_gbin, k_gbincount and k_gbins, and npair_ssa_kokkos.h:136 declares its own c_gbins.  Note also that npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87/91 copy atoms_per_bin and ghosts_per_gbin into members that are themselves never used.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead state that makes the class larger and misleads readers into thinking there is a resize/retry protocol like the one in NBinKokkos.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused members (and the corresponding allocations in the constructor and the two assignments in bin_atoms()).

summary: MinKokkos re-declares the iterate() return-code enum, hiding Min's identical enum in every KOKKOS min style, but omits MAXVDOTF -- so the values only agree by accident and MinFireKokkos silently falls through to the base enumerator.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.h:42-44 '// possible return values of iterate() method\n  enum{MAXITER,MAXEVAL,ETOL,FTOL,DOWNHILL,ZEROALPHA,ZEROFORCE,\n       ZEROQUAD,TRSMALL,INTERROR,TIMEOUT};' versus src/min.h:60-74 which declares the same eleven names plus 'MAXVDOTF'.  src/KOKKOS/min_fire_kokkos.cpp:234 'if (max_vdotf_negatif > 0 && vdotf_negatif > max_vdotf_negatif) return MAXVDOTF;' resolves through the derived enum to Min::MAXVDOTF only because MinKokkos has no member of that name.  The codes are consumed positionally by src/min.cpp:1024-1038 'char *Min::stopstrings(int n) { const char *strings[] = {...}; return (char *) strings[n]; }'.
failure_scenario: No wrong behavior today (the eleven shared enumerators happen to be in the same order). If anyone inserts or reorders an entry in Min's enum, the KOKKOS min styles keep the old numbering and Min::run() prints the wrong stop reason, or indexes stopstrings() out of range.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate enum from min_kokkos.h and use the inherited Min enum.
